newsitem.title: YUGOSLAVIA: Serbia acknowledges opposition won Belgrade poll.
newsitem.headline: Serbia acknowledges opposition won Belgrade poll.

text.p: Serbia acknowledged on Friday that opposition parties won a majority in nine municipalities in Belgrade in November 17 local elections but did not acknowledge its victory in other big towns.

In a letter from Foreign Minister Milan Milutinovic to the Organisation for Security and Cooperation in Europe (OSCE), Belgrade said the "coalition 'Zajedno' won the majority in nine municipalities in Belgrade".
But Milutinovic also said the authorities still needed more detail to clarify results in others towns.
The letter was sent as a response to an OSCE report by former Spanish prime minister Felipe Gonzalez who led a mission to Serbia to investigate the disputed elections.
Reuters obtained a copy of the letter which has yet to be made public in Belgrade.

The OSCE sent Gonzalez after an invitation from Serbian President Slobodan Milosevic, who has faced 46 days of protest over cancellation of the opposition victories in municipalities across the country.
But Milutinovic's letter said the results in Serbia's second biggest city, Nis, were still being studied.
"When competent authorities establish the facts, the results of the elections (in Nis) will be known," he said.

He said the opposition won the election in Uzice, Kragujevac and Zrenjanin but no party had won a majority in Pirot, Pancevo and Jagodina. Gonzalez's report had said the opposition had won the election in all these municipalities.
Milutinovic also called for more data relating to six other municipalities where Gonzalez said the opposition had won.

"For the purpose of verification, comparison and complete clarification it would be very useful if you could provide to our authorities the data you have at your disposal for the municipalities of Kraljevo, Smederevska Palanka, Vrsac, Soko Banja, Lopovo and Sabac," Milutinovic said.
The letter was addressed to Foreign Minister Niels Petersen of Denmark, which took over the chairmanship of the OSCE from Switzerland on January 1.

The OSCE's decision-making permanent council was called into special session on Friday to study Gonzalez's report and Milutinovic's reply, OSCE officials said. The meeting was due to start at 3 p.m. (1400 GMT).
The Yugoslav foreign minister said Gonzalez's call that the will of the people be respected was a position to which Belgrade was committed.
"However, it is obvious that all this should be established within the legal institutions, on the basis of law and regulations of the Republic of Serbia," he said.
But Milutinovic went on to say that Belgrade agreed with Gonzalez that all problems had to be solved "through implementation of adequate procedures and in a spirit of dialogue and cooperation".
